title: Login admission trusts the first forwarded address if it reaches the API
description: The unauthenticated login handler uses the first X-Forwarded-For item as its process-local rate-limit key. If an untrusted caller can select that item through a supported ingress path, the caller could use different budgets or consume a budget associated with another address. Admitted requests perform a user lookup and password verification, but the snapshot does not establish external reachability, effective ingress normalization, upstream limits, or a meaningful shared availability impact.
claimed_root_cause: The login handler accepts the first forwarded address as the limiter key without verifying that the immediate peer is trusted or that an ingress replaced caller-supplied values.

trace.description: The console proxy copies a present X-Forwarded-For header into its request to the API; POST is exported through this proxy.

The session login endpoint takes the first comma-separated forwarded value, falling back to the request peer when the selected value is empty, and passes the result to the limiter before issuing a session.
The process-local limiter maintains and enforces a separate event deque for each supplied key.
An admitted attempt looks up active users by normalized email and verifies either a dummy password hash for a non-unique result or the matching user's password hash.

evidence.description: Login input requires a bounded email and password and forbids extra fields.
Each application instance configures its login limiter for ten attempts per 60-second window per key.
The password hasher is configured with Argon2 time cost 3, memory cost 65,536 and parallelism 2.
The optional origin-signature boundary guards /api/v1 and /api/inbound/v1 prefixes, not /api/session/login.

The production-like Caddy configuration proxies API paths directly to the API and other unmatched paths to the console; this configuration alone does not establish the effective deployed forwarded-header chain.
The production-like overlay removes published API ports and also removes published console ports at line 82; the actual deployed network path is not established.
RelayPay describes itself as a synthetic payment-orchestration sandbox; the repository does not establish a hosted deployment.

blockers: The actual ingress topology and trusted-proxy settings are unknown, including whether an externally supplied first X-Forwarded-For item reaches either the API directly or the console proxy.
Effective upstream admission limits, process topology and shared login capacity are unknown, so a meaningful shared availability effect is not established.

validation_plan.deployment: Have the owner inspect the effective ingress routes and trusted-proxy configuration to determine whether an untrusted caller can control the first X-Forwarded-For value received by the API on a supported route. Have the owner inspect applicable upstream quotas, process topology and shared login capacity to assess whether independent budgets can affect operator login availability.

title: Metrics scrapes synchronously refresh database-wide gauges
description: When observability is enabled, an unauthenticated requester able to reach the scrape handler can cause database-wide counts and connector enumeration on the API's shared engine. Whether this causes meaningful contention with tenant operations depends on deployment access controls, data size and query cost.
claimed_root_cause: Each scrape synchronously refreshes operational gauges without a scrape-specific authentication, cache, rate or concurrency control visible in the application path.

trace.description: The catch-all proxy forwards GET requests using the supplied path; /backend/metrics targets the API's /metrics path.
If observability is enabled, the handler opens a transaction and refreshes gauges without a principal dependency; the transaction closes before rendering.
The refresh executes three mismatch counts, three queue counts and an unfiltered connector query, then updates gauges for each returned connector.

evidence.description: Observability defaults to disabled.
The production-like Caddy configuration routes /api/* and /health/* to the API and falls back to the console for other paths.
The optional origin signature requirement applies to selected API prefixes, not /metrics.
The API constructs one engine and session factory used by the scrape handler and application routes.
The production-like overlay removes the API host port mapping.

blockers: Effective observability enablement, external routing to the console proxy or scrape handler, and upstream authentication, rate and concurrency limits are not established by source.
Actual database cardinalities, query plans and competing workload determine whether the shared-engine work has meaningful impact; contention and recovery have not been observed.

validation_plan.local: In the approved isolated sandbox, instrument a small private dummy PostgreSQL fixture to confirm query count and connector rows processed per scrape, and inspect query plans without load or saturation.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner should inspect effective observability settings, routes and upstream scrape controls, then review existing database query and pool telemetry during normal scraping for contention and recovery. Do not generate availability stress.

title: Dispute submission body has no application-level size constraint
description: The synthetic dispute-network endpoint accepts an unauthenticated ZIP-typed request as a bytes body. If a lower-trust peer can reach the service without an effective body limit, sufficiently large requests could consume memory in the counterparty shared by approved operator submissions. A meaningful shared availability effect and lower-trust deployment access have not been established.
claimed_root_cause: The inbound route declares a complete bytes body without a source-visible request-size limit. The 20 MiB check applies to packages assembled by RelayPay, not independently submitted requests.

trace.description: POST /v1/submissions declares a bytes body and a required Idempotency-Key header without a route-level authentication dependency or body-size constraint.
The handler passes the package bytes and submission key to the resolved network.
The counterparty records a synthetic observation keyed by the submission key and includes the received byte length.

evidence.description: The application setup defines no admission middleware, and the submission body declaration has no size constraint.
The outbound package builder checks the assembled package against its 20 MiB limit; that check does not guard independent inbound requests.
The development service runs Uvicorn on all container interfaces and publishes port 8005. It inherits a 512 MiB memory limit and restart policy.
The API injects an HTTP dispute-network client into the admin router.
A first submission attempt calls the network submit method; a later attempt uses lookup.
The production overlay removes the dispute-network host port mapping.
The source Caddy configuration routes API and receiver paths and otherwise proxies to the console; it defines no dispute-network route.

blockers: The effective peer access controls, ingress body and concurrency limits, runtime memory behavior, and recovery consequences for a shared counterparty deployment are not established by the source snapshot. These determine whether a lower-trust requester can cause a meaningful effect on another operator submission.

validation_plan.deployment: The owner should inspect the effective deployment overlays, network and ingress policies, and runtime configuration to determine who can reach port 8005, whether body and concurrency limits apply before buffering, and how a counterparty interruption affects another operator submission and recovery. Do not probe or disrupt a deployed service.

title: Direct origin access can bypass edge admission
description: Direct origin callers bypass Worker replay, rate, body size and content-type checks if ingress allows access and signature enforcement is disabled. Origin merchant authentication and provider signature checks remain separate; unauthorized payments or webhooks are not established.
claimed_root_cause: Origin edge signature enforcement defaults to disabled.

trace.description: The origin exposes a customer endpoint under /api/v1.
When enforcement is false, requests skip signature verification and reach call_next at line 119.

evidence.description: Signature enforcement defaults to false.
The Worker applies admission and body checks before forwarding.
The Worker is optional and not deployed by this repository; lines 10-11 prescribe enforcement and restricted ingress.

blockers: Effective Worker routing, origin ingress, flag value and equivalent upstream limits are unknown; they determine exposure and shared impact.

validation_plan.local: In the approved sandbox, compare unsigned requests to a dummy FastAPI route with middleware enforcement false and true and a dummy secret; observe route reachability versus 401.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner inspects rendered Worker routing, effective flag, ingress policy and upstream limits, and identifies any affected shared resource; do not probe endpoints.

title: Queued webhook may stop reaching the origin after retry exhaustion
description: The optional edge returns 202 after archiving bytes and queueing a reference, before origin authentication or acceptance. If forwarding fails beyond the retry budget and neither the queue nor sender enables recovery, a valid synthetic connector event may remain unprocessed. Archived bytes alone do not establish complete event loss.
claimed_root_cause: The consumer retries unsuccessful forwards, while the checked-in local queue configuration sets max_retries to 3 without a dead-letter queue; no archive re-drive is present in the reviewed edge source.

trace.description: A POST matching the connector route enters the webhook handler.
The handler checks header shape, admission and body size, archives bytes, queues a reference and returns 202 before origin delivery.
The consumer acknowledges successful origin responses and requests retry for failed forwards; terminal handling is left to the queue platform.

evidence.description: The local consumer sets max_retries to 3 and specifies no dead_letter_queue.
Forwarding verifies archived bytes and treats only origin 2xx as success.
The origin enforces a provider timestamp window and HMAC, then checks the active connector and deduplicates events; an old queued signature can be rejected.
The edge is an optional local or CI proof and is not deployed by this repository.

blockers: Queue retention and terminal behavior after retry exhaustion, including any externally configured dead-letter or recovery mechanism, are not established by repository source.
An actual edge deployment, its effective queue settings and sender behavior after 202 are not established.

validation_plan.deployment: If an owner operates this edge, ask them to inspect the effective queue consumer, dead-letter, retention and recovery settings and the sender's retry policy after a 202. Ask them to observe existing records or operational evidence for failed deliveries and recovery without generating audit traffic.

title: Queue retries origin responses that may be permanent
description: A requester can submit a webhook with shaped headers and an invalid provider signature for queuing. If the queue redelivers an origin-rejected message, each delivery can cause another archive read and origin request, potentially consuming shared capacity.
claimed_root_cause: The consumer treats every non-2xx origin response as retryable and requests a fixed two-second delay.

trace.description: The route checks header shapes and admission, then archives and queues the body without verifying the provider signature.
The consumer reads and verifies the archived body, signs an origin request and returns false for non-2xx responses.
A false result requests a retry after two seconds.

evidence.description: Admission uses the connector and event ID as its coordinator key and enforces timestamp, replay-key and configured rate checks.
An invalid provider signature raises 401 before the connector database lookup.
The local queue configuration specifies three retries; deployed settings and delivery behavior are not established.

blockers: The source does not establish a reachable deployment, effective upstream quotas, deployed queue retry settings or redelivery behavior, or whether the extra work materially affects shared capacity.

validation_plan.deployment: An owner should inspect the effective route, upstream quotas, queue consumer and retry settings, and existing aggregate queue and origin telemetry to determine whether rejected messages are redelivered and whether the extra work materially affects shared capacity. Do not send test traffic.

title: Durable Object replay admission depends on storage input-gate semantics
description: If requests can interleave between the coordinator's storage reads and write, identical replay keys could both be admitted, causing two synchronous origin forwards or two webhook queue entries. This does not establish duplicate financial effects.
claimed_root_cause: Replay and rate state are read before a combined write without an explicit transaction or concurrency guard; whether requests can interleave depends on Durable Object runtime semantics.

trace.description: Routes API requests and connector events to admission.
Validates the replay-key shape and sends it with the timestamp and limits to the named coordinator.
Reads replay and rate state before writing both and allowing the request.

evidence.description: The configured coordinator uses SQLite storage; line 5 specifies the compatibility date.
Admission precedes synchronous forwarding at line 101 and webhook queueing at line 116.
The origin checks webhook timestamp and signature and deduplicates connector events.
Payment intent creation uses a scoped principal and an idempotency key.

blockers: The available isolated coordinator capabilities do not specify a Durable Object runtime emulator, so actual storage input-gate interleaving cannot be established by the widened-gap mock.
The effective Worker route and runtime compatibility configuration are not established by the source snapshot.

validation_plan.local: With a compatible isolated Durable Object runtime, send a bounded pair of concurrent identical requests with a valid dummy replay key and timestamp to one coordinator, compare with a sequential pair, and count forwards to a dummy origin.
validation_plan.deployment: Ask an owner to observe the effective Worker route and compatibility configuration and identify the runtime input-gate semantics applicable to these storage operations.

title: Caller-selected event IDs partition webhook admission state
description: A caller who can reach the optional Worker can submit shape-valid webhook headers and select a different coordinator for each event ID before provider authentication. Accepted requests write coordinator keys and can archive distinct bodies and enqueue references. This could consume resources shared with other users, but deployment exposure and meaningful shared impact remain unknown.
claimed_root_cause: Webhook admission selects a Durable Object using the connector ID and caller-supplied event ID, with no source-visible aggregate admission budget or cleanup of the coordinator's replay and minute-bucket keys.

trace.description: A POST to the connector events path reaches the webhook handler.
Provider headers are shape-checked, then connector ID and caller-supplied event ID select the admission coordinator.
After admission and a one MiB body check, the Worker archives a new body digest and queues a reference.

evidence.description: The coordinator checks timestamp, replay key and per-object minute limit, then writes replay and rate keys; the class contains no cleanup.
The origin checks the provider HMAC before accepting the inbound event.
The local configuration disables workers_dev and configures a rate limit of 60 and replay window of 300 seconds.
The Worker is optional and is not deployed by this repository.

blockers: Owner-observed routing and bindings are needed to establish whether untrusted callers can reach the Worker with its coordinator, archive and queue attached.
Upstream limits, account quotas, storage lifecycle and recovery, and resource sharing are outside the source and determine whether the allocation pattern has meaningful shared impact.

validation_plan.deployment: Ask the owner to inspect existing route and binding configuration, upstream limits, account quotas, storage lifecycle and affected resource sharing without sending traffic or changing resources.

title: Receiver buffers webhook bodies before signature validation
description: A requester able to reach the webhook and supply its three required headers can cause the application to request the complete body before timestamp and signature validation. A current timestamp also reaches an HMAC operation that concatenates the timestamp prefix and body. Large or concurrent requests could consume memory in the shared receiver process, but a service interruption and its recovery have not been demonstrated. Invalid signatures are rejected before JSON parsing or receipt insertion.
claimed_root_cause: The webhook calls request.body() without an application-level byte-counted admission limit before authenticating the request. The reviewed Caddy and Uvicorn configuration does not specify a per-request body limit; the configured container memory limit is process containment, not a request-size rejection policy.

trace.description: The configured Caddy route forwards /webhooks/relaypay to the receiver without an explicit body-size policy.
The POST route requires event ID, timestamp and signature string headers but does not authenticate them before entering the handler.
The handler requests the complete body before calling receive_event for timestamp and signature validation.

evidence.description: Timestamp parsing and freshness checks occur after the handler has obtained the body.
A current timestamp reaches HMAC construction that concatenates the timestamp prefix and body.
Signature rejection precedes JSON parsing and receipt insertion.
After authentication, the receiver stores a body digest and deduplicates by event ID; unauthenticated durable receipt growth is not established.
Service defaults specify restart-unless-stopped and limits of one CPU and 512M memory.
The separate receiver inherits those defaults and runs Uvicorn without an explicit request-size or concurrency setting.
The production-like overlay removes the receiver's directly published port; the Caddy configuration still routes the webhook to it.
The installed HTTP metrics middleware does not configure a body-size limit.

blockers: Actual receiver exposure, effective ingress and server body-byte, concurrency and receive-time limits, container isolation, and recovery after resource exhaustion are deployment facts. No meaningful shared interruption has been demonstrated.

validation_plan.local: In the approved isolated sandbox, use a bounded mocked ASGI fixture with small body chunks and no Content-Length to observe when bytes are consumed relative to validation; inspect the installed server and framework receive path for applicable bounds. Do not create memory pressure.
validation_plan.deployment: Have the owner inspect effective routing and ingress, proxy and server body-byte, concurrency and receive-time limits, including chunked requests. Review receiver resource isolation and restart behavior in configuration and existing operational records; do not probe or stress a live endpoint.

title: Inbound queue draining can delay other tasks in the shared scheduler
description: The inbound endpoint can add eligible events to a queue that the synchronous poller drains before running later scheduled tasks. The drain has no batch-start cutoff, claim count limit, or deadline, so arrivals during a drain can extend it. Source does not establish that a lower-trust sender can sustain accepted work long enough to cause meaningful shared delay, or that deployed admission and worker topology permit that effect.
claimed_root_cause: The shared poller claims inbound events until no eligible row remains, with no fairness boundary on the total work performed before it proceeds to later tasks.

trace.description: The connector event HTTP endpoint accepts a request body and provider event ID, timestamp, and signature headers, then passes them to admission.
Admission checks timestamp freshness and an HMAC, requires an active connector, and stores a new connector and event-ID pair as pending.
Each claim selects the oldest currently eligible event globally, using a row lock and lease, without a batch-start cutoff.
The worker repeatedly claims and processes eligible events until a claim returns none.
The scheduler calls the inbound drain synchronously before later due tasks and before outbox publication; the next loop iteration also waits for it to return.

evidence.description: Freshness and HMAC checks precede insertion. The HMAC covers timestamp and body, but not connector ID or provider event ID; exploitation without the secret would require access to a still-fresh valid signed request and an accessible route.
The connector must be active. An existing connector and event-ID pair is treated as a replay when its body digest matches, while a new pair is inserted as pending.
A database uniqueness constraint covers connector ID and provider event ID; it does not impose an aggregate queue limit.
Claims use SKIP LOCKED, LIMIT 1, and a 30-second default lease. These bound an individual claim and support recovery, but do not cap the enclosing drain.
Handler failures have delayed retries and default to dead-lettering after three recorded attempts; this does not bound the number of distinct eligible events.
The ordered schedule places inbound processing before authorization expiry and PSP event application. Earlier scheduled tasks can also be delayed in the next iteration.
The task's next deadline is advanced after the synchronous call returns. Outbox publication follows the scheduled-task loop and has its own 100-item cap.
The optional edge validates header shape and body size and applies admission keyed by connector ID and event ID. Its deployment and effective aggregate limit are not established by source.

blockers: Source does not establish that an independently controlled lower-trust sender has the commerce signing secret, or can obtain a still-fresh valid signed request and reach an admission path.

Meaningful shared delay depends on accepted arrival rate, processing throughput, effective ingress controls, and whether independent workers continue the affected tasks. Those deployment facts are not established by the sanitized source.

validation_plan.local: In the approved isolated sandbox, submit a small finite set of dummy signed events, add one new event while a drain is in progress, and record claim order and the point at which dummy expiry and PSP runners execute. Use a private database and mocked external effects; do not test saturation. This can verify scheduling and admission behavior but cannot establish deployment impact.
validation_plan.deployment: Have the owner review sender trust and access to fresh signed requests, routing and effective aggregate admission limits, normal accepted-event and drain rates, and worker topology or independent scheduling for expiry, PSP application, and publication. Review existing configuration and operational evidence without generating live load.

title: Optional observability ports may be reachable outside the operator network
description: If a deployment enables the optional observability profile and permits access from outside the operator network, an unauthenticated network client could reach Prometheus or anonymous Grafana and obtain operational information. Source does not establish that such a deployment or route exists. API operational gauges additionally require OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED to be true and relevant data to exist.
claimed_root_cause: The production overlay resets core service port mappings but has no corresponding overrides for the optional observability services, whose base mappings specify host ports without a host IP.

trace.description: The optional Prometheus service publishes container port 9090 on host port 9090 without specifying a host IP.
The overlay resets core service and simulator ports but contains no override for Prometheus, Grafana, or the collector.
Prometheus is configured to scrape the API's internal /metrics endpoint and service and worker metrics.
When OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED is true, the endpoint refreshes and renders operational gauges; otherwise it returns 404.
The gauges include unscoped mismatch and queue counts and connector public identifiers with circuit states.

evidence.description: The optional collector publishes host ports 4317 and 4318; the same profile publishes Prometheus 9090 and Grafana 3001.
Grafana enables anonymous Viewer access, disables the login form, and publishes host port 3001.
The provisioned Grafana datasource uses proxy access to the internal Prometheus service.
The configured OTLP receivers listen on all container interfaces, and the configuration specifies no authentication extension.
Deployment prerequisites call for only ports 80 and 443 to accept inbound traffic and for SSH to be restricted to operators; the source does not establish actual network policy.
The documented production startup enables the edge profile, not the observability profile.
The documentation warns that enabling observability retains its host ports and advises private binding or leaving the profile disabled.

blockers: The sanitized source does not establish whether an actual deployment enables the observability profile, its effective bindings and observability settings, or whether host and cloud network controls permit a lower-trust client to reach the published ports.

validation_plan.deployment: The owner should inspect the actual enabled profiles, rendered host bindings, OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED setting, and attached host and cloud network policies to determine whether a principal outside the intended operator network can reach the observability ports.

title: Connector version revocation does not govern inbound admission
description: A sender retaining the shared commerce control key can submit a fresh event for an active connector after a connector version is revoked. Whether that sender should lose inbound authority on version rotation is unresolved.
claimed_root_cause: Inbound admission uses a shared commerce control HMAC key and checks connector status without consulting connector version or credential status.

trace.description: The connector event route accepts a connector ID, event ID, timestamp, signature and request body.
The route passes the commerce control secret to admission.
After timestamp and HMAC checks, admission selects an active connector without consulting version status and stores a fresh event as pending.

evidence.description: Version creation generates a credential, stores it encrypted and digested, and returns it.
Activation requires a verified pending version and revokes the previous active version.
The documented inbound HMAC key is COMMERCE_CONTROL_SECRET.

blockers: The source does not establish whether version revocation is intended to withdraw inbound authority from a sender that retains the separate shared key, or whether such a sender is permitted to retain it.

validation_plan.deployment: Ask the owner to inspect the connector contract and intended key distribution policy to determine whether a revoked version's sender may retain the shared inbound key and submit events. Do not contact a deployed endpoint.

title: Connector webhook bodies are buffered before authentication
description: A caller able to reach the connector webhook can supply the required headers and cause the origin to buffer the request body before provider timestamp and signature validation. If effective request-size and concurrency limits permit sufficient buffering, requests could exhaust API worker memory and interrupt service. The optional edge also buffers the body before applying its one-MiB check. The source snapshot does not establish that the availability consequence is achievable in a deployment.
claimed_root_cause: The origin route and optional origin-signature middleware read the request body without a source-visible streaming byte limit before authentication. The optional edge checks its body limit after arrayBuffer completes.

trace.description: The POST connector event endpoint accepts a connector ID and requires provider event, timestamp, and signature headers.
The route reads the body before calling accept_inbound_webhook for timestamp and signature validation.

evidence.description: Timestamp parsing and freshness checks and then HMAC verification occur after the route passes the buffered body to the service; connector lookup follows successful signature validation.
When origin-signature enforcement is enabled for this path, the middleware reads the body before verifying the edge signature.
The optional edge validates connector and header shapes and performs admission before reading the body; line 111 applies the one-MiB limit only after arrayBuffer resolves.
The source-visible Caddy API route proxies requests without a configured request-body limit.

blockers: The source snapshot does not establish whether an actual deployment exposes the origin or edge route to an unauthenticated caller, or its effective ingress and runtime body-size, concurrency, and memory limits. These facts determine whether buffering can produce a meaningful availability effect.

validation_plan.deployment: Have the owner inspect the connector route's actual network attachment, effective ingress and server streaming body limits, edge admission configuration, concurrency limits, and workload memory limits. Do not send traffic to deployed endpoints.

title: Connector webhook event identity is not bound to its signature
description: A party that obtains a valid signed connector webhook within its replay window may be able to resubmit the same timestamp and body under a different event ID. Source indicates that this creates a separate queued event and can cause an earlier capture to be applied after a refund to a synthetic commerce payment link. The resulting state transition has not been observed.
claimed_root_cause: The connector webhook HMAC covers the timestamp and body, while the connector ID and provider event ID used to route and deduplicate the event are supplied separately.

trace.description: The inbound HTTP endpoint accepts the connector ID in the path and the event ID, timestamp, and signature in separate headers.
The service verifies the timestamp and body HMAC, selects an active connector, and deduplicates by connector and supplied event ID before creating a pending event.
The worker claims queued events and passes their payload and event ID to commerce synchronization.
The handler selects a payment link by the payload payment ID and applies capture or refund status without an event ordering or deduplication guard.

evidence.description: The uniqueness constraint covers connector ID and provider event ID, not authenticated payload identity.
The timestamp must fall within the configured replay window; an existing event ID with different payload bytes is rejected.
A capture sets the link to PAID; a refund sets the link and order to REFUNDED. The exact resulting order state after replay remains unobserved.
The optional edge validates header shape and applies replay-key admission scoped by connector and event ID; its forwarding path preserves the supplied provider event ID.
The optional origin boundary verifies an edge signature for inbound paths when configured; effective ingress routing is not established by source.
The separate PSP simulator documents at-least-once delivery and a timestamp-and-body signature. It is a distinct path and does not establish connector delivery guarantees.

blockers: The required bounded observation of the connector acceptance, worker processing, and resulting dummy commerce state was not performed. The prior runtime request was rejected by the provider safety filter, and the narrowed scope prohibits retrying execution.

Source does not establish that a lower-trust actor can obtain and resubmit a valid request within the replay window through the actual ingress, or establish the connector producer's delivery guarantees. No deployed route or ingress configuration is established.

validation_plan.local: An authorized owner can use an isolated, bounded fixture to verify that identical signed capture bytes with a different event ID produce a separate accepted event, then process it after a dummy refund and inspect the single dummy payment link and order. Stop after recording the observed statuses.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner should review the actual connector producer, transport and ingress configuration to determine delivery guarantees, who can observe and resubmit a signed request within the replay window, and whether any control binds the event ID to authenticated bytes.

title: Console proxy buffers POST bodies before backend admission
description: The console catch-all POST handler reads the complete request body before invoking the backend and contains no handler-level authentication or body-size check before that read. If sufficiently large or concurrent requests can reach it, body buffering could consume shared console process resources and affect other users. No availability impact has been demonstrated.
claimed_root_cause: The proxy awaits request.bytes() before forwarding the request and has no handler-level body-size limit.

trace.description: The catch-all route exports proxy as its POST handler.
For a POST, proxy awaits request.bytes() while constructing the backend fetch, before that fetch is invoked.

evidence.description: The supplied Caddy configuration sends remaining paths, including /backend paths, to the console and declares no request-body limit.
The development Compose layout publishes the console port on the host.
The supplied Next.js configuration specifies standalone output and security headers but no explicit request-body limit.
The console declares Next.js 16.4.2; the effective request handling limit for this route remains unverified.
The optional edge worker handles /api/v1 paths and returns 404 for other unmatched paths; its body check does not establish a limit for the console /backend route.

blockers: The effective ingress and Next.js runtime body-size, concurrency and timeout limits for requests reaching this handler are not established. The stated isolated execution capabilities do not establish availability of the pinned Next.js standalone server and its dependencies for a local runtime check.
The shared-process effect and recovery under the effective limits are unobserved; source inspection alone does not demonstrate an availability impact.

validation_plan.deployment: If a deployment exists, an owner should inspect the actual route attachment, ingress and hosting body-size, concurrency and timeout settings, Next.js runtime limits, console process resource limits and restart policy. Determine whether the combined limits bound per-request and aggregate buffering without sending load to the deployment.

title: Requester-controlled HTTP labels may accumulate in shared metrics
description: The API records unmatched request paths and HTTP methods as metric labels. The linked local fixture reports retained children in the shared middleware, but it did not measure process memory or demonstrate degradation. If an ingress permits enough distinct requests to reach a shared API process, accumulated labels could consume resources needed by other users.
claimed_root_cause: The API and shared ASGI metrics middleware use the raw path when no route template exists and pass the request method unchanged to a process-global Prometheus registry without application-level label normalization or eviction.

trace.description: The supplied production-like Caddy configuration forwards /api/* paths to the API.
After a response, the API middleware falls back to request.url.path when no route is present and passes request.method to the metrics observer.
The shared middleware applies the same route fallback and method passthrough.
The observer uses method and route as counter and histogram label values.

evidence.description: operations_metrics creates and returns a module-global OperationsMetrics instance.
OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED gates the shared scrape handler; the observation middleware has no corresponding enablement check.
The optional origin signature guard covers /api/v1 and /api/inbound/v1 prefixes, leaving paths such as /api/probe-missing/a outside that guard.
The supplied service defaults specify a 512M memory limit; the API inherits those defaults.
The production-like overlay resets the API's directly published ports.

blockers: The snapshot does not establish whether an untrusted client can reach a running instance, or what upstream request limits and process recovery settings apply. Those facts determine whether label growth can have a meaningful shared effect in an actual installation.

validation_plan.deployment: If an installation exists, ask its owner to inspect the effective route to the API, upstream request and rate limits, process memory limit, and worker recycling or restart policy. Do not send traffic to the installation.

title: Unmatched paths can create distinct durable usage rollups
description: A requester reaching the API middleware can supply distinct unmatched paths that may create durable anonymous rollup rows in shared database storage. Whether this can cause meaningful shared resource growth depends on ingress and storage controls not established by the snapshot.
claimed_root_cause: The middleware uses the raw path when no route matches and passes it with the method to an hourly upsert. The service truncates these values but does not normalize their cardinality or prune rollups.

trace.description: HTTP requests reaching the API enter the middleware before route authentication.
The route key falls back to the request path when no route object is present.
Except for health and metrics paths, the middleware passes the route, method and optional principal scope to record_request and catches persistence exceptions.
The hourly PostgreSQL upsert includes the truncated route and method in its key.

evidence.description: The telemetry contract calls for route templates, bounded request logs and durable hourly rollups.
UsageRollup is described as low-cardinality durable evidence and its unique key includes route and method.
The probabilistic retention operation deletes RequestLog rows rather than UsageRollup rows.
The supplied Caddy configuration forwards /api/* to the API without a rate limit in that file.
The optional Worker requires an API-key-shaped bearer value and admission before forwarding synchronous requests.

blockers: Effective ingress routing and admission, quotas, rollup storage limits and any external cleanup are not established by the source snapshot; their effect on meaningful shared resource growth and recovery is unknown.

validation_plan.local: With the isolated python_pg fixture, create the two observability tables, start create_app with dummy settings, send two distinct unmatched GET paths through its HTTP interface and inspect the anonymous rollup keys; stop after observing the rows.
validation_plan.deployment: An owner should inspect ingress admission and quotas, rollup storage limits and cleanup policies, and aggregate anonymous rollup cardinality and age with read-only, non-sensitive queries. Do not generate load.

title: Expiry may miss a void committed after its query snapshot
description: A merchant with payments:write can initiate a void for its scoped authorised, uncaptured payment after the hold has elapsed if expiry has not changed the payment status. Expiry excludes non-failed voids in the same statement that locks payment rows. It remains unverified whether PostgreSQL can select the payment using a stale absence result when the void commits between that statement's snapshot and its attempt to lock the payment. If that occurs, expiry can leave verified successful void evidence unable to transition the payment from expired to cancelled. The potential effect is confined to synthetic payment state and operation convergence; no ledger corruption or cross-tenant effect is established.
claimed_root_cause: Expiry does not separately recheck void rows after acquiring the payment lock. Void initiation inserts the void under that lock without changing the payment status or version, while the transition helper rechecks only those payment fields. Whether this produces the claimed race depends on the actual PostgreSQL execution and locking behavior.

trace.description: The merchant void endpoint requires payments:write and passes the principal's organisation and environment to void initiation.
The service locks the scoped payment and checks for a succeeded authorization, no capture and authorised payment status; it does not check whether the hold has lapsed.
The service inserts a PROCESSING void and operation within the transaction without changing the payment status or version.
The expiry statement excludes non-failed voids and selects payment rows FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; the subsequent loop does not separately recheck void rows.
The transition helper rereads payment status and version and permits authorised-to-expired, without checking void rows.
Verified successful void evidence requests a transition to cancelled. If the payment is already expired, the transition is rejected and the finalization transaction rolls back.

evidence.description: The non-failed-void exclusion is part of the locking statement, and the selected payments are passed directly to transition.
Void admission requires no capture and an authorised payment, without testing the authorization expiry time.
The transition helper's locked reread selects only payment status and status version.
The database transition list permits authorised-to-expired and does not include expired-to-cancelled; its trigger checks the status pair.
The outcome application path catches transition or database errors during finalization and records an apply failure.
The existing expiry test creates an in-flight void before calling expiry; it does not exercise the proposed snapshot-to-lock interleaving.
The engine construction does not explicitly specify an isolation level.

blockers: The decisive PostgreSQL snapshot-to-lock interleaving and its effect with SKIP LOCKED have not been observed. Source alone does not establish that the actual query can retain the stale void-absence result.

The prior delegated runtime validation was rejected by the provider safety filter before execution. This assignment prohibits further execution or sandbox requests, so no local reproduction was performed.

validation_plan.local: An owner may use an isolated PostgreSQL fixture with a dummy scoped authorised payment whose hold has lapsed. Establish the expiry statement snapshot, arrange for void initiation to commit under the payment lock before expiry attempts that lock, and observe whether expiry selects and expires the payment despite the committed PROCESSING void. If it does, apply locally constructed verified success evidence through the native finalizer and inspect the transaction outcome. Also check a void still holding the lock and a void committed before the expiry snapshot. Use no provider or shared service.

title: Portfolio metrics may expose tenant-derived values to a broader reader
description: An authorized portfolio request writes its organisation and environment's analytics into shared process gauges. A lower-trust reader who can reach the enabled metrics endpoint and attribute a refresh to that scope could observe those values.
claimed_root_cause: Scoped portfolio results are copied into shared gauges without organisation or environment labels, and the metrics handler renders the registry without a principal check.

trace.description: The portfolio endpoint resolves an active environment in the principal's organisation with technical:read or admin scope, then refreshes metrics.
The selected scope is recalculated and its values are written to shared gauges.
When observability is enabled, the endpoint refreshes operational gauges and renders the shared registry without a principal dependency.

evidence.description: Scope resolution checks permission, organisation ownership and active environment status.
Portfolio gauges have no tenant or environment labels; completion has only a kind label.
The metrics accessor returns a process-wide singleton.
Observability defaults to disabled.
The production overlay removes the API host port.
The checked-in Caddy API route matches /api/* and /health/*, not /metrics.

blockers: The effective deployment configuration and network or scraper access policy are unknown. Source does not establish that a lower-trust reader can reach an enabled metrics endpoint and attribute a value to a particular tenant and environment.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated bounded fixture with dummy data for two scopes, compare authorized portfolio results with same-process metrics scrapes after each refresh; do not infer external accessibility.
validation_plan.deployment: An owner should inspect the effective observability setting, API bindings, routing, firewall and scraper permissions, and determine whether a less-trusted reader can observe and attribute a tenant refresh without accessing sensitive values.

title: PSP callback reads the request body before authentication
description: A client able to reach the PSP callback can submit a body that the API reads in full before checking the provider or its signature. If effective ingress and concurrency limits do not sufficiently bound these requests, concurrent requests could consume memory shared with other API users. The source does not establish an actual deployment route, effective limits, or a meaningful shared availability effect.
claimed_root_cause: The PSP route calls request.body() without a source-visible streaming size cap before provider authentication. When origin-signature enforcement is enabled for this path, its middleware also reads the full body before verifying the origin signature.

trace.description: The POST /api/inbound/v1/psp/{provider} route accepts a request without a provider authentication dependency.
The route reads the complete request body before passing it to provider validation and signature verification.

evidence.description: The API installs the optional origin-signature middleware and includes the PSP router in the same application.
The inbound path is guarded when origin signatures are required; the middleware reads the body at line 107 before verifying the signature and may reject the request before it reaches the route.
After the route supplies the body, the inbox rejects unsupported providers and then verifies the simulator signature and replay window before parsing or storing the event.
Missing provider authentication headers are rejected before HMAC verification, but this check occurs after the route has read the body.
The production-like Caddy configuration proxies API paths without an explicit request-body limit in this file.
The optional edge worker routes connector webhooks and merchant v1 paths; a PSP callback falls through to a 404, so its connector webhook limit does not establish a PSP limit.
The development API command starts Uvicorn without an explicit request-body size or concurrency setting.

blockers: The active route to the API, effective request-size and concurrency limits across ingress and server layers, shared process topology, and recovery behavior are not established by the sanitized source. These facts are decisive for meaningful shared impact.

validation_plan.deployment: An owner should inspect the actual PSP route and effective streaming and chunked body-size limits, concurrency limits, API worker sharing and process recovery configuration. Determine whether the combined limits can materially affect other API users without probing a live service.

title: A snapshot missing its category can produce a non-escalated risk review
description: The snapshot response schema accepts an arbitrary snapshot object. If a clean snapshot lacks category, the category checks assign CRITICAL severity but no hard-stop classification, and contribute 20 risk points when its catalogue is present. With no other points or hard stops, the total is LOW and the review is completed. The shipped site service supplies a category in every fixture, so source does not establish that a lower-trust party can produce this input or that a configured service returns it. No merchant activation or payment bypass is established.
claimed_root_cause: check_category classifies a non-HOME_GOODS string as PROHIBITED_CATEGORY but classifies an absent or non-string category as NONE. execute_review derives escalation from hard-stop classifications and the total score band, rather than the individual check severity.

trace.description: The configured site service supplies an HTTP response whose snapshot object is accepted without a category-specific schema.
The fetched snapshot is stored and passed into the prepared review.
Deterministic checks run on the prepared snapshot; hard-stop eligibility is determined from classifications.
An absent category yields classification NONE, CRITICAL check severity and zero earned category points.
A review without a hard stop or HIGH or CRITICAL total band is marked COMPLETED.

evidence.description: The review route requires CSRF validation and workflows:write permission in the resolved organisation and environment; its request accepts a fixed set of site references.
The strict response envelope defines snapshot as dict[str, object], without requiring category.
The shipped synthetic fixture starts with HOME_GOODS; the prohibited-category fixture replaces it with another string.
Missing and non-string category values are classified NONE despite CRITICAL check severity; a non-HOME_GOODS string is classified PROHIBITED_CATEGORY.
A missing category also loses the content-matches-category points; a present catalogue can retain its ten points.
The total combines deterministic risk contributions and validated model findings; model findings or other risk factors can change the outcome.

blockers: The source-supported site service contains only immutable synthetic fixtures, all with string categories. It does not establish that a lower-trust party can omit category or influence a configured replacement service.

The repository does not establish whether any actual configured snapshot service can return an omitted or non-string category, or whether such a response represents an actionable merchant risk decision.

validation_plan.local: In the approved isolated sandbox, use a private dummy database and a fake SiteSnapshotSource returning a clean synthetic snapshot with category removed and a valid empty model result. Run prepare_review and execute_review once, then inspect the dummy review status, score and findings. Compare with the same snapshot using a non-HOME_GOODS string. This tests the conditional behavior, not exposure through the shipped fixture service.
validation_plan.deployment: Without contacting a service from this review, ask the owner to inspect the configured source contract and data provenance: whether omitted or non-string category values are possible, whether a lower-trust party can influence them, and whether completed reviews affect an actual authorization or operational decision.

title: Empty or short registrant names can pass the identity consistency check
description: A configured HTTP snapshot source can return a snapshot whose nonempty merchant name and empty registrant organization pass the deterministic identity consistency check. A short registrant organization also passes when it occurs within the merchant name. This suppresses that check's IMPERSONATION hard stop, although other checks or model findings can still cause escalation. Source does not establish that a lower-trust party can influence those fields in a configured service.
claimed_root_cause: The case-folded bidirectional substring comparison accepts an empty registrant organization and has no minimum meaningful overlap requirement.

trace.description: The configured HTTP source fetches and validates a response containing a snapshot object without field-level validation of its contents.
The fetched snapshot is stored for the organisation and environment and supplied to the prepared review.
The review runs deterministic checks over the prepared snapshot.
For a nonempty merchant name, an empty registrant organization satisfies substring containment and produces a NONE identity-consistency classification rather than IMPERSONATION.

evidence.description: SiteSnapshot validates the outer response but declares snapshot as an arbitrary dictionary.

The review route requires CSRF validation and workflows:write permission in the resolved organisation and environment; its request selects one of six site references rather than supplying snapshot fields.
A configured RISK_SITE_BASE_URL selects the HTTP snapshot source; otherwise the in-process deterministic source is used.
The shipped service describes immutable code-defined snapshots with no uploads or crawling.
The base fixture supplies a nonempty registrant organization.
The check requires a nonempty merchant string but does not require a nonempty organization before bidirectional case-folded substring comparison.
A consistent result receives classification NONE and five points; an inconsistent result receives IMPERSONATION.
IMPERSONATION is a hard-stop classification.
Deterministic hard-stop classifications set the review hard-stop flag. Other deterministic checks and model findings may independently set it.
The review is escalated on a hard stop or HIGH or CRITICAL overall severity; otherwise it is completed.

blockers: Source does not establish whether a configured snapshot service can return empty or short registrant organizations under a lower-trust party's influence. The shipped service returns fixed synthetic fixtures.

validation_plan.deployment: Without probing a deployed service, ask the owner to inspect the configured snapshot source and its documented data flow for a synthetic onboarding: determine whether a lower-trust party can cause whois.registrantOrganization to be empty or a short substring of identity.merchantName and whether that value reaches the review unchanged. No production or shared data mutation is required.

title: Pricing outlier scoring relies on the snapshot-provided median
description: The pricing check uses medianPricePaise from the fetched snapshot. If it is absent or non-positive, the check reports no extreme outlier and awards all 10 available points; a sufficiently high supplied median can also prevent an outlier from being counted. This can reduce the calculated risk contribution by up to 10 points. The shipped synthetic snapshot service supplies fixed values, so source does not establish that a lower-trust party can cause either condition in a configured environment.
claimed_root_cause: check_pricing accepts the catalogue's supplied median without checking it against the item prices and leaves the outlier count at zero when the median is missing or non-positive.

trace.description: The configured HTTP snapshot service returns a response whose snapshot object is accepted without a catalogue-specific schema.
The fetched snapshot is stored and subsequently supplied to the review.
The check reads medianPricePaise from the catalogue and counts outliers only when it is a positive integer.
A zero outlier count earns all 10 points, including when no usable median was supplied.

evidence.description: The response model validates the outer fields but declares snapshot as an unconstrained dictionary.
The review endpoint requires a principal, CSRF validation and workflows:write permission, and accepts a fixed site reference rather than a caller-supplied snapshot.
The shipped merchant-site service describes immutable, code-defined snapshots with no uploads or crawling.
The shipped PRICE_OUTLIER fixture includes both the high-priced item and a positive median that makes it detectable.
The pricing risk contribution is the maximum less earned points; the outlier classification is not among the hard-stop classifications.

blockers: Source does not establish whether any configured HTTP snapshot service permits a lower-trust party to omit or manipulate the median independently of the catalogue prices.

validation_plan.local: In an approved isolated sandbox, pass dummy catalogue prices containing a clear outlier to check_pricing with a missing median and with a high supplied median; compare the classifications and earned points with a valid reference median. This verifies the conditional behavior but does not establish external reachability.
validation_plan.deployment: An owner should inspect the configured snapshot provider's contract and data provenance, without sending live requests, to determine whether a lower-trust party can control or omit the median independently of item prices. If so, assess whether a review's score affects an actual decision.

title: Unverified model source path can suppress a finding’s hard stop
description: A structured provider can return a verbatim claim quote labeled html. If its classification is not independently corroborated by a deterministic check, the service assigns LOW confidence and suppresses that finding’s hard stop. Other hard stops or a HIGH or CRITICAL total can still escalate the review. The shipped route defaults to a deterministic fake provider; source does not establish a reachable attacker-controlled provider or a real provider that emits this relabeling. No payment or merchant-activation bypass is established.
claimed_root_cause: The service uses the model-returned sourcePath to assign confidence, while validation checks the quote against the whole redacted snapshot without verifying its location.

trace.description: The service receives structured output from the findings provider for a delimited snapshot.
Validation requires each quote to occur in the redacted snapshot but does not bind it to sourcePath.
An uncorroborated html-labeled finding receives LOW confidence and cannot set a hard stop; final escalation also depends on other findings and total severity.

evidence.description: The default provider derives findings deterministically from the snapshot; the route accepts an injected provider at router construction.
The review endpoint requires CSRF validation and workflows:write permission in the resolved organisation and environment.

blockers: Source does not establish that a configured findings provider can be influenced by a lower-trust party or emits html for a claim-derived quote. The shipped fake attributes findings to their top-level snapshot key.

validation_plan.deployment: An owner can inspect the actual provider wiring and sanitized synthetic onboarding outputs to determine whether claim text is lower-trust and whether the provider can misattribute its source. Do not probe a live provider.

title: Recurring-failure replay disclosure is unreachable through the shipped route
description: The duplicate-consumption branch contains an unscoped attempt lookup, but the claimed operator-facing disclosure is blocked before intake: the route passes an ISO-formatted string to a strict Python-mode envelope validator that requires an aware datetime object.
claimed_root_cause: The consumption marker does not compare the stored payload digest on a duplicate, and the duplicate intake branch looks up an attempt by the replay-supplied provider attempt ID without tenant or invoice predicates.

trace.description: A principal can submit a recurring-failure request for an invoice; the handler requires CSRF and resolves workflows:write or admin permission and the principal's active environment.
The handler loads the submitted invoice using organisation, environment, and public ID predicates, then derives an event ID from the scope and idempotency key.
The handler validates a Python dictionary containing now.isoformat() as occurredAt. Strict envelope validation rejects that string before the intake call and response.

evidence.description: The envelope enables strict validation and declares occurredAt as AwareDatetime.
If called directly with a valid envelope, duplicate consumption leads to an attempt lookup filtered only by provider_attempt_id; the resulting object is returned to the caller.
The consumption marker stores the supplied digest, but an IntegrityError rolls back the savepoint and returns False without comparing the existing digest.
Consumption markers are unique on consumer_name and event_id and separately store payload_sha256.
The attempt model makes provider_attempt_id globally unique.
Administrative scope resolution requires the requested permission or admin scope and an active environment belonging to the principal's organisation.

The direct integration fixture supplies a Python datetime to envelope validation; source search found direct intake callers in tests and the administrative route, but no other shipped producer or consumer that exposes the returned attempt.

reason: A bounded isolated check using the target envelope model rejected a route-shaped dictionary with a datetime_type error at occurredAt; replacing only that value with an aware Python datetime was accepted. The promoted observation is agents/terra_verify_replay_r2/artifacts/result.txt. Consequently the first request cannot reach the consumption marker or the claimed response through the identified route. The unscoped direct-service lookup remains a source-level defect, but no source-visible lower-trust direct caller and disclosure boundary establish the proposed impact.
